q: At what common temperature, would a block of wood and a block of metal feel equally cold or equally hot when touched?
a: When the temperature of the object is equal to that of the human body, no transfer of heat takes place between the body and the object. Thus, when the temperature of the block of wood or block of metal is equal to 37°C, i.e., the temperature of the human body, these appear equally hot or cold on touching on account of non-transfer of heat.

q: Why an ice box is constructed with a double wall?
a: An ice-box is made of double wall and the space between the walls is filled with some non-conducting material to provide heat insulation, so that the loss of heat is minimized.

q: Pieces of copper and glass are heated to the same temperature. Why does the piece of copper feel hotter on touching?
a: We know that copper is a far better conductor of heat than glass. When we touch the hot copper piece, it transmits heat readily to the hand. But this is not in the case when the hot glass piece is touched.

q: Place a safety pin on a sheet of white paper. Hold the sheet over a burning candle until the paper becomes yellow and chars. Now shake off the pin. It will leave a white trace on the paper. Explain this phenomenon.
a: This is due to the reason that the pin, being a good conductor of heat, takes heat from the paper under it and gives away to the surroundings. As a result of this, the paper under the pin is comparatively colder than its remaining part.

q: 7. If air is a bad conductor of heat, why do we not feel warm without clothes?
a: Ans.: Air is a poor conductor of heat. Moving air carries heat due to convection. Thus, when we are without clothes, the moving air in contact with our bodies carries away the heat from our bodies and hence we feel cold.

q: 8. Why do we prefer white or light coloured clothes in summer than dark coloured clothes?
a: Ans.: White or light coloured clothes absorb the least heat from the Sun and hence keep us comfortable in summer. On the other hand, dark coloured clothes absorb more heat from the Sun and keeps us hot in summer. Thus we prefer white or light coloured clothes in summer more than dark coloured clothes.

q: 9. The water table varies from place to place. Why?
a: Ans.: Water table is the upper level of the Earth's layer where water is found. The water found below the water table is known as groundwater. The availability of groundwater or the level of water table depends on the amount of rainfall and recharge conditions in an area, e.g., in places near the river, one may obtain water after digging only a few feet, while one may have to dig several feet down in a desert before you get water. Thus, the water table varies from place to place.

q: 10. There is abundance of water on our planet Earth. Why is there a scarcity of water then?
a: Ans.: Although there is abundance of water on our planet Earth, but only a very small fraction of water is fit for consumption. More than 97% of water that exists the Earth is in seas and oceans that is highly salty and unfit for drinking or other purposes.

q: 1. What differences can you find between a clinical thermometer and a laboratory thermometer?
a:
Ans.: The clinical thermometer is smaller. It measures only from 35°C to 42°C. It is mainly used for medical purposes. There is a small bend or kink in the capillary tube. This prevents the mercury from coming down, when the thermometer is taken out of patient's mouth. Thus the doctor can read the temperature after removing the thermometer.
The laboratory thermometer is larger than clinical thermometer and it is used to measure temperature from 0°C up to 100°C or more in the laboratory. It has no kink in its capillary tube.

q: 5. Can convection take place in solids? Why?
a: Ans.: No. The molecules in a solid are only free to vibrate about their fixed positions. For convection to take place, the molecules need to move carrying the heat with them. Hence convection can not take place in solids.

q: 6. In winters, when the Sun suddenly goes behind the clouds we feel cold. Can you say why?
a: Ans.: The clouds cut off the radiant heat from the Sun.

q: 7. Why do fire fighters wear special shiny suits when they enter a burning building?
a: Ans.: The shiny suits reflect heat. This protects them from fire when they enter a burning building.

q: 8. If you live on the top floor of a building, you must have noticed that, in summer the roof gets very hot. Suggest a few ways by which people who live on the top floor of a building can protect themselves from the radiant heat of the Sun?
a: Ans.: The roof top may be painted white so as to reflect the radiant heat from the sun. If green or white Perspex sheets are used on a roof they prevent the main roof from absorbing the radiant heat of the Sun. Watering the roof and maintaining a rooftop garden are the other ways to protect from the heat of the Sun.

q:
9. (a) What is water table?
(b) What is groundwater?
(c) What is an aquifer?
a:
Ans.: (a) If we dig a hole in the ground, we find moist soil at certain depth. On further digging, we reach a depth at which all spaces between the soil particles and cracks in the rocks are filled with water. The upper limit of this depth is called the water table.
(b) The water found beneath the earth's surface and below the water table is called groundwater.
(c) At places beneath the earth's surface, the groundwater is stored between layers of hard rocks below the water table. This is known as an aquifer. Water in the aquifers can be pumped out with the help of tubewells or hand pumps.

q: 14. At a camp site there are tents of two shades - one made with black fabric and the other with white fabric. Which one will you prefer for resting on a hot summer afternoon? Give reason for your choice. Would you like to prefer the same tent during winter? (NCERT Exemplar)

q: 15. Why is it advised not to hold the thermometer by its bulb while reading it? (NCERT Exemplar)

q: Two test tubes with water are heated by a candle flame as shown in figure. Which thermometers (Figure (a) or figure (b)) will record a higher temperature? Explain.

q: Why are hollow bricks used to construct the outer walls of houses in hot regions?
answer: Hollow bricks trap air inside them. Air is a poor conductor of heat, so it prevents outside heat from entering the house, keeping it cool.

q: Explain how large water bodies prevent extreme temperature in areas around them.
answer: Water has a high specific heat capacity. It absorbs and releases heat slowly, which moderates the temperature of the surrounding coastal areas, causing sea and land breezes.

q: Explain how water seeps through the surface of the Earth and gets stored as groundwater.
answer: Water from rain and other sources seeps through the porous soil and rocks. This process is called infiltration. The water collects over impermeable rocks underground, forming an aquifer.

q: The water cycle helps in the redistribution and replenishment of water on the Earth. Justify the statement.
answer: The water cycle involves evaporation, condensation, and precipitation. It continuously moves water from oceans to land and back, redistributing it across the globe and replenishing freshwater sources like rivers and groundwater.
